label: koto ha nai
title_raw: ことはない ([ことはない] )(koto ha nai)
title: ことはない
meaning: no need to 〜しなくても　いい
meaning_example: There's no need to be insulting, you know!

notes.text: 動−辞書刑　＋　ことはない
notes.html: 動−辞書刑　＋　ことはない

examples.japanese: ただの風邪ですから、心配することはありません
examples.body_text:
ただの風邪ですから、心配することはありません 

		Its just a common cold, so 
		there's no need to 
		worry.
examples.body_html:
ただの風邪ですから、心配することはありません 
Its just a common cold, so there's no need to worry.

examples.japanese: この世に思いわずらうことはない。
examples.body_text:
この世に思いわずらうことはない。 

		I 
		don't 
		have a care in the world.
examples.body_html:
この世に思いわずらうことはない。 
I don't have a care in the world.

examples.japanese: 時間は十分あるから急ぐことはない。
examples.body_text:
時間は十分あるから急ぐことはない。 

		There is 
		no need to 
		hurry as we have plenty of time.
examples.body_html:
時間は十分あるから急ぐことはない。 
There is no need to hurry as we have plenty of time.

examples.japanese: ちょっと待たされただけで、なにもそんなに怒ることはないでしょう。
examples.body_text:
ちょっと待たされただけで、なにもそんなに怒ることはないでしょう。 

		You only had to wait a little bit, so 
		there's no need to 
		get so upset.
examples.body_html:
ちょっと待たされただけで、なにもそんなに怒ることはないでしょう。 
You only had to wait a little bit, so there's no need to get so upset.

examples.japanese: 君があやまることはないよ。
examples.body_text:
君があやまることはないよ。 

		There is no need for you to apologize.
examples.body_html:
君があやまることはないよ。 
There is no need for you to apologize.

comments.text:
Is this right? Shouldn`t it be 〜ことではない

〜ことはない　means that thing isn`t or doesn`t exist but ではない means its not that kind of thing.



I don`t think I have heard a native speaker use ことはない





jyubun　can also mean enough or sufficent. so # could be translated as



because there is sufficent time, there is no need to hurry.
comments.html:
Is this right? Shouldn`t it be 〜ことではない
〜ことはない　means that thing isn`t or doesn`t exist but ではない means its not that kind of thing.

I don`t think I have heard a native speaker use ことはない

because there is sufficent time, there is no need to hurry.

comments.text: I hear this grammar pattern used by native speakers all the time. I'd say it's the number one way to say there's no need/it's not necessary.
comments.html: I hear this grammar pattern used by native speakers all the time. I'd say it's the number one way to say there's no need/it's not necessary.

comments.text: 「必要はない」and「ことはない」have the same meaning.
